quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?

options.text: Only passengers
All riders and passengers
No one

questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on operating your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Stay out of truck blind spots. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then re-apply the brake with steady, controlled pressure.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:

options.text: A tire check.
A test of the turn signals.
A paint inspection.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. A paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers the traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding ________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

options.text: On the expressway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. At intersections, position yourself in your lane to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far part of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Has no impact on safety and is neither encouraged nor discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far part of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. Where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid hazards like opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases collision danger. Riding on the far side may encourage them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does your steering feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is low.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight at all times is the most effective way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: What should you do if a vehicle is tailgating you?

options.text: Allow them to pass.
Speed up.
Do not change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at an even higher speed.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?

options.text: By the left footrest.
By the right footrest.
By the right handle grip.

questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: At night, how can you tell if the road ahead has bumps when riding behind another vehicle?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
Look at the rear bumper to see if it is bouncing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bouncing up and down.
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
The front and rear brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.
Protects your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When entering a turn, when should you change gears?

options.text: Before the turn.
During the turn.
Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: How can you help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on day and night when it is legal and safe. Use your high beam to help others see you. Running lights also help with visibility.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding?

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective materials on your clothing also help other drivers see you.
